x: Risk is a Discord bot for running a server: moderation, levels, an economy, tickets, logs, giveaways, stream alerts and a website dashboard where staff change settings without typing commands. These pages explain what it can do, how each part works and how to use it. 571 commands in 13 categories, 57 message variables. Where to start # New to Risk? Read Getting started to add the bot and set up t

This page takes you from nothing to a working server in a few minutes. You need the Manage Server permission on the server you want to add Risk to. 1. Add Risk to your server # Use the Add to server button on the main site. Pick your server and keep every permission ticked. Risk asks only for what its features need, and a missing permission is the most common reason a command fails. Open your ser

The dashboard is a website where staff change Risk's settings. Everything you can save there is also stored by the bot, so changes take effect right away and the commands and the dashboard always agree. Signing in # Type !dashboard in your server, or open the dashboard link from the main site. Choose Sign in with Discord and approve the request. Risk only asks to see your account and the list of

Risk has 60+ moderation commands plus automatic filters. Every moderation command checks the permission of the person using it, and Risk also needs the matching permission itself and a role above the member it acts on. Warnings, timeouts, kicks and bans # Goal Command Warn and record it !warn @user reason See or remove warnings !warnings @user , !delwarn , !clearwarnings @user Stop someone talkin

Members earn XP by chatting. XP adds up to a level, and levels can hand out roles. How XP works # Each message earns 15 to 25 XP, multiplied by your server's multiplier. A member can earn XP at most once per cooldown (60 seconds by default), so spamming doesn't help. The level for a total is the whole number part of the square root of XP divided by 100. In other words, reaching level n takes 100

Every member has a wallet and a bank in each server. Coins earned in one server stay in that server. Getting started # !balance shows your wallet and bank. !daily pays 500 coins and adds 50 more for every day in a row, up to a bonus of 1,000 (the streak keeps going if you claim again within 48 hours). It can be claimed about once a day. !work pays out once an hour, and !weekly and !monthly pay bi

Tickets are private support channels. A member presses a button on a panel, Risk creates a channel only they and your staff can see, and staff close it when it is done. Set it up # Make a category for tickets and a staff role. Run !ticket "category_id" @staff in the channel where you want the panel. Risk posts a message with an Open ticket button. Run !setlogs #ticket-logs so closed tickets and t

Server logs write what happens in your server into a channel, so staff can see who deleted a message, who joined, who got a role and what moderators did. Turn logging on # Make a private channel for staff, like #server-logs . Run !logs #server-logs . Risk starts posting events there. Run !logtest to check it works, and !logstatus to see the settings. What is logged # Events are grouped into categ

Smaller features that make a server feel alive. Giveaways # !giveaway start 30m 1 Steam gift card runs a giveaway for 30 minutes with one winner. People enter with a reaction or button. !giveaway end , !giveaway cancel , !giveaway reroll , !giveaway list and !giveaway info manage them. !giveaway drop starts a quick first-to-claim drop. !giveaway require <id> @Member limits a giveaway to a role, a

Risk can greet people when they join and say goodbye when they leave. Set up a welcome message # !welcome #welcome {embed} Welcome New_user to {server}! You are the {ordinal} member. {embed} Write New_user where the new member should appear. In a normal message it becomes a mention. Inside an embed it shows their bold name and a normal mention is sent above the embed, so they still get notified.

Risk announces when someone in your server, or a streamer you follow, goes live. The alert is an embed titled "<name> is live" with a link to the stream. When the stream ends, Risk posts a "stopped streaming" embed with how long it lasted. Turn it on # !streamalerts #streams @StreamPing picks the channel. The role at the end is optional. Turn alerts off with !streamalerts off . !streamrole @Strea

Info # !ping checks the response time, !uptime shows how long Risk has been online, !botinfo shows its stats, !invite gives the link to add it, !prefix shows or changes the server prefix, !dashboard gives the dashboard link and !tos and !privacy show the policies. Server and user info # !serverinfo , !userinfo , !roleinfo , !channelinfo , !avatar , !banner , !servericon , !serverbanner , !memberc

Several features send a message you write yourself: welcome and leave messages, level-up messages, auto-replies, custom commands and the VIP welcome DM. You can drop variables into any of them, and Risk fills in the real values when the message is sent. The basics # A variable is a word in curly braces, like {server} . If you write Welcome to {server}, {name}! We now have {server.members} members

Variables are placeholders you type inside a message. Risk swaps each one for the real value when the message is sent. They work in welcome and leave messages, level-up messages, auto-replies, custom commands and more. The message templates page explains where each one works. There are 57 variables. Type !variables in Discord for the same list, !variables Server for one group, and !testvars <mess

Command rules let staff decide who can run commands, where, and how often. They live in the dashboard under Commands , and they have two layers: basic rules for every command and command rules for one command at a time. Members with the Manage Server permission (or Administrator) ignore every rule, so staff can never lock themselves out. !help and !dashboard are never blocked by basic rules eithe

VIP is an optional upgrade for a single server. Everything in Risk works without it. VIP adds extra commands, scheduled announcements, embed-style auto-replies and a custom accent colour, and the higher plans add tools for running big communities. The plans # There are four plans. Prices and checkout links are on the VIP page of the main site. Basic is paid monthly and is the base. It unlocks sch

Each command below says which plan it needs. A plan includes the commands of the plans under it: Basic is in everyone's, White is in White, Supreme and Lifetime, Supreme is in Supreme and Lifetime, and the Lifetime-only commands are only in Lifetime. Check what your server has with !vipcommands . Basic commands # Every VIP plan includes these. !vipcolor # Needs Manage Server VIP. Sets the accent

Every command Risk has, grouped by category. This list is generated from the bot itself, so it always matches what is available. 571 commands in 13 categories, 57 message variables. Commands start with ! , ? or , unless your server added its own prefix. Use the search box at the top to find any command by name or by what it does. Info 11 commands Status, help and links. Moderation 62 commands Kee

Risk checks Discord permissions every time you run a command. This page lists which permission each command asks of you, and what Risk needs for itself. What Risk needs # When you add Risk, keep the default permissions ticked. These are the ones features rely on: Send Messages, Embed Links, Attach Files and Add Reactions for nearly everything. Manage Messages for !clear , auto-mod and deleting co

Risk doesn't answer a command # Check the prefix. The defaults ! , ? and , always work. If staff set another prefix, that works too. Check that Risk can see and send messages in that channel. The command may be switched off or restricted. Ask staff to look at General and Commands in the dashboard and the command rules . Risk tells you when a rule blocks you. Wait a moment and try again.
